title: Qu'est-ce que je ressens?
oneGoal: Students will identify and name basic emotions (happy, sad, angry, scared) in French
decisionPoints: How comfortable are students talking about feelings?
What visual supports help with emotion vocabulary?
How to create a safe space for sharing?
progression: Foundation lesson introducing emotional awareness and basic vocabulary
realWorldConnection: Knowing how we feel helps us communicate our needs and get help when needed

title: Mon visage montre mes émotions
oneGoal: Students will recognize emotions in facial expressions and connect faces to feelings
decisionPoints: Are students connecting faces to emotions?
What emotion faces are most relatable?
How to address different cultural expressions of emotion?
progression: Builds on Lesson 1 by adding visual recognition of emotions through facial expressions
realWorldConnection: Reading faces helps us understand how others feel and respond appropriately

title: Mon corps ressent aussi
oneGoal: Students will identify where emotions are felt in the body (heart racing, tight tummy, etc.)
decisionPoints: How are students connecting body sensations to emotions?
What body awareness activities work best?
Are all students comfortable with body talk?
progression: Builds on Lesson 2 by exploring how emotions manifest physically in our bodies
realWorldConnection: Understanding body signals helps us recognize our emotions early

title: Toutes les émotions sont normales
oneGoal: Students will understand that all emotions are normal and acceptable to feel
decisionPoints: How to validate all emotions without judgment?
What examples resonate with student experiences?
How to address 'bad' vs 'uncomfortable' emotions?
progression: Builds on Lesson 3 by normalizing all emotions and reducing emotional shame
realWorldConnection: Accepting our emotions helps us feel better about ourselves and handle difficult feelings

title: Dire mes sentiments
oneGoal: Students will practice expressing emotions using simple French phrases
decisionPoints: Which phrases are most useful for students?
How to encourage shy students to share?
What communication methods work beyond verbal?
progression: Builds on Lesson 4 by providing language tools to express accepted emotions
realWorldConnection: Telling others how we feel helps us get support and understanding

title: Quand je suis content
oneGoal: Students will explore positive emotions and appropriate ways to express joy
decisionPoints: How do students show happiness appropriately?
What activities bring students joy?
How to channel excitement positively?
progression: Builds on Lesson 5 by focusing specifically on positive emotions and their expression
realWorldConnection: Expressing happiness appropriately helps us share joy with others

title: Quand je suis triste
oneGoal: Students will learn healthy ways to cope with sadness and seek comfort
decisionPoints: How comfortable are students with sadness?
What comforting strategies work for this age?
How to normalize crying and seeking help?
progression: Builds on Lesson 6 by exploring sadness and healthy coping strategies
realWorldConnection: Learning to handle sadness helps us feel better and connect with others who care

title: Quand je suis fâché
oneGoal: Students will learn appropriate ways to express and manage anger
decisionPoints: How do students currently handle anger?
What calming strategies are age-appropriate?
How to address aggressive responses to anger?
progression: Builds on Lesson 7 by focusing on anger management and healthy expression
realWorldConnection: Managing anger appropriately helps us solve problems and keep friendships

title: Quand j'ai peur
oneGoal: Students will identify fears and learn strategies to feel brave and seek help
decisionPoints: What fears are common for this age group?
How to address fears without dismissing them?
What brave strategies can students use?
progression: Builds on Lesson 8 by exploring fear and developing courage and help-seeking
realWorldConnection: Learning to handle fear helps us try new things and stay safe

title: Respirer pour me calmer
oneGoal: Students will learn simple breathing exercises to self-regulate emotions
decisionPoints: Which breathing techniques work best for 6-year-olds?
How to make breathing exercises engaging?
Are students able to use breathing when upset?
progression: Builds on Lesson 9 by introducing concrete self-regulation tools
realWorldConnection: Deep breathing helps us feel calmer anytime, anywhere

title: Comprendre les autres
oneGoal: Students will begin to recognize and respond to emotions in others
decisionPoints: How well can students read others' emotions?
What empathy skills are developmentally appropriate?
How to encourage kind responses to others' feelings?
progression: Builds on Lesson 10 by extending emotional awareness to understanding others
realWorldConnection: Understanding others' feelings helps us be good friends and family members

title: Aider un ami triste
oneGoal: Students will learn how to comfort and support friends who are upset
decisionPoints: What helping strategies are appropriate for this age?
How to teach helping without fixing?
When should students get adult help?
progression: Builds on Lesson 11 by practicing specific empathy and helping skills
realWorldConnection: Helping friends when they're sad makes us good friends and builds strong relationships

title: Mes stratégies émotionnelles
oneGoal: Students will identify their personal toolkit of strategies for managing different emotions
decisionPoints: Which strategies work best for each student?
How to personalize emotional regulation tools?
Are students able to choose appropriate strategies?
progression: Builds on Lesson 12 by creating personalized emotional regulation toolkits
realWorldConnection: Having our own strategies helps us handle emotions independently

title: Mon journal des émotions
oneGoal: Students will create their emotions journal showing their learning and strategies
decisionPoints: How can students best show their emotional growth?
What format works for different learners?
How to celebrate emotional learning achievements?
progression: Builds on Lesson 13 by synthesizing all emotional learning into a personal journal
realWorldConnection: Keeping track of our emotions and strategies helps us continue to grow

title: Émotions en musique
oneGoal: Students will explore emotions through music and songs
decisionPoints: Which songs help students express emotions?
How does music help with emotional regulation?
What musical activities are most engaging?
progression: Extension: Uses music as an additional tool for emotional expression and regulation
realWorldConnection: Music helps us express and process our emotions in fun ways

title: Art des émotions
oneGoal: Students will create art to represent different emotions and feelings
decisionPoints: How can art help students process emotions?
What art materials work best for emotional expression?
How to support all artistic abilities?
progression: Extension: Provides creative outlets for emotional expression and processing
realWorldConnection: Art gives us ways to show our feelings when words aren't enough

title: Jeux d'émotions
oneGoal: Students will play games that practice emotion recognition and regulation
decisionPoints: Which games are most effective for emotion practice?
How to keep games inclusive and supportive?
What games help with specific emotional skills?

realWorldConnection: Playing emotion games helps us practice skills in a fun, safe way

title: Histoires d'émotions
oneGoal: Students will explore emotions through stories and characters

What discussion questions deepen emotional understanding?

title: Émotions en famille

decisionPoints: How to honor diverse family approaches to emotions?
What family sharing is appropriate and safe?

title: Célébration des émotions
oneGoal: Students will celebrate their emotional growth and commit to using their new skills
decisionPoints: How can we celebrate emotional growth appropriately?
